name: Bayesian Inference Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday bayesian inference work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical bayesian inference tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday bayesian inference work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical bayesian inference tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When multiple bayesian inference strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen bayesian inference approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Prefer the simplest bayesian inference approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Before starting bayesian inference work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
5. When bayesian inference decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Keep bayesian inference outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. State assumptions about bayesian inference explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. When bayesian inference guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Validate bayesian inference outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
10. Keep bayesian inference changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
11. Check that bayesian inference terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting bayesian inference assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of bayesian inference correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated bayesian inference concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop bayesian inference edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about bayesian inference over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
